open_points.subject: source-supplied datetime acceptance and normalization
open_points.text: “kept as supplied: the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC” leaves “their accepted forms and checks” to States 6–7 without stating them here
open_points.question: Which datetime forms are accepted for source-supplied instants, and must an offset-aware non-UTC value be normalized to naive UTC or refused?
options: Accept any offset-aware datetime, convert the instant to UTC, then remove the offset
Accept only UTC-aware datetimes and refuse other offsets
Also accept naive datetimes by interpreting them as UTC
open_points.default_guess: Accept offset-aware datetimes, normalize to UTC, remove tzinfo for persistence, and refuse naive input.

witness.initial: An authorized producer submits a valid snapshot whose approved_at is 2026-11-08T10:00:00+02:00.
events: The import validates the source-supplied datetime.
outcomes: The import accepts it and stores 2026-11-08 08:00:00 as naive UTC.
The import refuses it because only an explicitly UTC input form is accepted.
witness.observer: The producer sees acceptance versus a typed rejection.

open_points.subject: wall-clock read timing and operation coverage
open_points.text: “An operation reads the clock once” and “where in an operation its one clock read happens, are the accepted spec's, carried to States 6–7” do not identify which failed or read-only invocations count as operations that read it or the point at which they do so
open_points.question: For every operation, including early refusals and operations that write no portal-owned timestamp, exactly when is the wall clock read, and which such invocations take no operation-level reading?
options: Read once immediately on entering every application operation, including early refusals
Read only after preliminary validation or authorization establishes that current time or a fresh timestamp is needed
Specify the read point separately for each operation contract
open_points.default_guess: Specify it per operation and defer the read until the first time-dependent decision, while reusing that value thereafter.

witness.initial: A staff-login request presents a well-formed token envelope but an incorrect password; the failed-login audit writer will append its own audit record.
events: The caller submits the failed login.
outcomes: The login operation reads the wall clock at entry and the audit writer reads it again: two readings.
The login operation never needs its own instant and only the audit writer reads: one reading.
witness.observer: A counting clock source and its Required test see different call counts.

open_points.subject: CLK-002 exclusivity verification
open_points.text: CLK-002 requires that “the clock source is the only reader of the host's wall and elapsed clocks”, but its source check only forbids imports of `time` and calls to `datetime`/`date` `now`, `utcnow`, or `today`
open_points.question: What check demonstrates that no other host-clock path—such as `os.clock_gettime`, a database time function/default, another library, or an indirect alias—reads time outside the clock source?
options: Enumerate and prohibit every permitted host-clock API and database time expression outside the source
Instrument all host-clock boundaries in tests and fail on any read outside the source
Narrow CLK-002 to only the specifically enumerated Python APIs
open_points.default_guess: Keep the broad invariant and combine an exhaustive source-policy check with instrumented database and host-clock boundaries.

witness.initial: The audit writer calls the injected clock source once but discards its result; its insert lets a database `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` default populate occurred_at.
events: An operation appends an audit record.
The counting clock source reports the required one audit-writer call.
The database independently reads its host clock while inserting the record.
outcomes: The stated source and counting checks pass even though CLK-002 is false and occurred_at may differ from the injected reading.
A check covering database clock expressions rejects the implementation.
witness.observer: The invariant checker and readers of the audit timestamp see the difference.

open_points.subject: CLK-002 witness binding
open_points.text: The Required tests define CLK-002, but the witness line binds only CLK-001: “CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal]”
open_points.question: Which existing witness check is bound to CLK-002 and asserts its required source, counting, boundary, and viewer-entry behavior?
options: Bind CLK-002 to one existing verification check that covers the complete item
Bind its source, wall-clock, audit, and elapsed-clock clauses to several named checks
open_points.default_guess: Use separate named checks for static source exclusivity, wall/audit counts, and the viewer-entry elapsed-clock boundary.

open_points.subject: security-review dependency surface
open_points.text: A31 says the dependency category affects only “deploy/requirements.txt (fastapi, pydantic, argon2-cffi, uvicorn pinned)”, while A32 now makes every distribution installed in the built image and the release gate part of the vulnerability decision
open_points.question: Does the security review's dependency category cover only the four direct pins, or every installed transitive distribution plus the built-image release gate required by A32?
options: Keep the A31 affected set limited to the four direct pins
Expand A31 to the complete installed distribution set, built image, OSV data acquisition, and release gate
open_points.default_guess: Expand the affected set to match A32.

witness.initial: The image contains the four clean direct pins and a transitively resolved distribution whose installed version has a non-withdrawn OSV vulnerability.
events: The security review inventories the affected dependency surface.
The pre-deploy gate evaluates the image.
outcomes: Reading A31 literally, the review records only the four direct pins as affected.
Reading A32, the transitive distribution and image-bound release gate are also affected and the deploy is blocked.
witness.observer: The security reviewer sees different coverage; the deployment operator sees whether the transitive vulnerability is within the reviewed control.

open_points.subject: matching installed distributions to OSV packages and versions
open_points.text: “an OSV entry that is not withdrawn lists its installed version as affected” and “unmatchable advisory data” do not define distribution-name normalization, version interpretation, or what makes data unmatchable
open_points.question: How is an installed distribution identified and matched to an OSV PyPI package/version, and which missing, malformed, or noncanonical metadata conditions make the deploy fail closed?
options: Use PyPI/PEP 503 name normalization and the ecosystem's standard version semantics; fail if an installed distribution lacks a matchable name or version
Require an exact textual package-name and version match and fail every non-exact case
Let the selected OSV tool's matching behavior define normalization and unmatchable cases
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical PyPI name normalization and standard Python version semantics, and fail closed when an installed distribution cannot be represented or evaluated.

witness.initial: A built image contains distribution metadata named `Foo_Bar` version `1.0`; the OSV copy identifies the PyPI package as `foo-bar` and lists version 1.0 as affected.
events: The release gate matches them against its OSV copy.
outcomes: A normalizing matcher treats the names as the same package and blocks the deploy.
An exact-text matcher treats the advisory as unmatchable, with the text leaving whether that blocks or is ignored to implementation.
witness.observer: The deployment operator sees a vulnerability block versus a different matching/refusal result.

open_points.subject: deployment-procedure handoff
open_points.text: “The tool that runs the check is a deployment procedure, not a portal rule, carried to the deploy route” names neither a receiving state nor a confirming check
open_points.question: Which later state owns the concrete image enumeration, single-copy OSV acquisition, image-content binding, and service-start gate, and which check confirms that execution?
options: Assign the complete procedure to a named deployment state with the dependency release-gate witness
Keep the procedure in State 2 and specify it here
Name an existing deploy-route artifact and its verification check as the receiver
open_points.default_guess: Assign it explicitly to the deployment-route state and confirm it with `verification:dependency_release_gate_client_portal`.
